title: The S Salon & Academy: Where Personal Beauty Is an Art
excerpt: Discover The S Salon & Academy, a salon known for personalized hair treatments, bridal makeup, nail art, handmade Ayurvedic products, and professional beauty training.
body:
IBC Belleza Luxé | Beauty & Lifestyle Feature

Every head of hair carries a story. Some tell of a long-awaited transformation, others of damage that needs patient repair, and some simply ask for a fresh beginning. At The S Salon & Academy, every one of those stories is heard before the first scissor is lifted.

A Philosophy Built on Listening

In an industry that often rushes from chair to chair, The S Salon has chosen a slower, more thoughtful path. Every visit begins with a personalized consultation, a conversation about your hair, your skin, your lifestyle, and what you want to feel when you look in the mirror. Nothing is one-size-fits-all, and no look is copied from a template.

It is this belief, that great beauty is personal, that has earned the salon its reputation. Guests consistently speak of the friendly, knowledgeable team, the calm, relaxing atmosphere, and the care taken with damaged hair in particular.

Hair, Reimagined

The salon's hair menu is as complete as it is skilled. Precision haircuts, rich colour, highlights, and sun-kissed balayage sit alongside restorative and smoothing treatments: hair spa, botox, kerafine, nanoplastia, and vegan protein therapy.

For clients with tired, over-processed strands, this is where the salon shines. The focus is not only on a style that turns heads, but on hair that is healthier, stronger, and glossier long after the appointment ends.

Glow, From Head to Toe

Beauty at The S Salon extends well beyond the hair. The team offers:

  • Facials that refresh and revive the skin
  • Pedicures and gel nail extensions for polished, lasting finishes
  • Mehendi artistry, intricate and celebratory
  • Bridal and party makeup, designed to make every client feel like the most radiant version of herself

For brides in particular, the salon's attention to detail turns a big day into a calm, confident experience.

Rooted in Nature

The salon's care continues at home through its handmade in-house range: Ayurvedic hair oil, rosemary spray, day cream, night gel, and lip balm. Each product reflects a simple idea, that traditional ingredients and a gentle touch still have an important place in modern beauty routines.

The Academy: Where Passion Becomes a Profession

What truly sets The S Salon apart is its Academy. Here, aspiring beauty professionals receive hands-on training shaped by the same values the salon lives by: skill, creativity, and genuine care for the client. The Academy turns talent into careers and carries the salon's standards into the next generation of stylists and artists.

The Belleza Luxé Verdict

The S Salon & Academy is more than a place for a new look. It is a place to be listened to, cared for, and understood. Whether you come for a bridal transformation, a hair repair journey, or simply a well-deserved pause, you leave feeling seen.

Be Seen. Be Cared For. Be You.

title: Fashion Trends in India: Where Tradition Meets Ease
excerpt: From comfort-first couture to heritage fabrics, here is how India is dressing this winter wedding season.
body:
Indian fashion is in a confident, expressive phase. Designers, brands and everyday wearers are leaning toward clothes that look rich and feel effortless. Winter, the busiest wedding season of the year, shows this most clearly.

The Wedding Season Sets the Pace

India's 2026 winter wedding season is projected to see around 52 lakh weddings in just 25 days. That scale makes the season a catwalk for the whole country. What brides, grooms and guests wear now shapes what shows up in stores and on social feeds for months afterwards.

Comfort Meets Glamour

The biggest idea this season is that grand outfits no longer have to feel heavy. Outfits are designed to look luxurious while staying light, breathable and easy to wear, even when layered. Lightweight lehengas are a good example. They keep the embroidery and drama, but the wearer can still dance through the night. 

Bridal: Less Excess, More Expression

At India Couture Week 2026, the message from the runway was clear. Bridalwear is becoming less about excess and more about personal expression, with pieces that are easier to wear and move in. Ivory and white are also growing in popularity, and they are counted among the biggest bridal statements of 2026.

For many brides, this means choosing a silhouette that suits them instead of the heaviest outfit in the shop.

Shape Over Fabric

Velvet remains a winter favourite, but fashion writers note that the real hero of 2026 is shape, and simpler cuts are winning. This explains the rise of hybrid silhouettes such as the sharara-gharara with its double-flare bottom, called one of the newest trends in Indian wedding fashion. Clean lines, fluid drape and one well-placed detail now carry more weight than layers of ornament.

Colour and Jewellery

The season's palette moves between three families: soft pastels such as dusty rose and powder blue, deep jewel tones, and metallics. For jewellery, matha pattis, pearl and polki headbands, diamond minimalism and heritage gold are all in demand. Jewel tones and metallics also tend to photograph well, which matters in a wedding culture built around reels and albums.

Menswear Gets Thoughtful

Men's fashion is moving in the same direction, toward sharp tailoring and meaningful fabrics. Sherwanis in zari, floral and pastel styles are popular, and a handwoven khadi kurta pyjama with a classic Nehru jacket is a suggested look for grooms in 2026. Handloom and heritage textiles are becoming a style statement as well as a nod to craft. 

Smart Layering for Winter

One practical tip keeps coming up in winter style guides. A heavily embroidered or velvet dupatta can double as a shawl, so no separate wrap is needed. It keeps the outfit unbroken and the look cohesive.

The Takeaway

Indian fashion today is not about choosing between heritage and modernity. The strongest looks keep the craft, colour and embroidery that make Indian clothing special, but cut them in ways that suit real life. Whether you are the bride, a guest or simply someone who loves to dress well, the rule of the season is the same: wear what makes you feel beautiful and comfortable.

title: The Runway Begins Here: Meet Omansh Gupta
excerpt: Nine years old and in Grade 3, Omansh Gupta is just beginning to discover what it feels like to own a room. His first runway walk came at a school Trash-to-Fashion competition. From there, he stepped into IBC Super Kids, a talent hunt for children aged 3 to 12, and found a new kind of excitement. With a family rooted in the event world and a confidence that is growing with every step, Omansh’s story is not about titles. It is about a young star finding his stride.

<p class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:auto;mso-margin-bottom-alt:auto;
line-height:normal;mso-outline-level:3"><b><span style="font-size:13.5pt;

mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:none;mso-fareast-language:EN-IN;mso-bidi-language:
HI">Omansh Gupta, 9, on his first runway walk, a talent hunt debut, and the
confidence of beginning</span></b><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:
"Times New Roman",serif;mso-fareast-font-family:"Times New Roman";mso-font-kerning:
0pt;mso-ligatures:none;mso-fareast-language:EN-IN;mso-bidi-language:HI"></span></p>

line-height:normal"><i><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:"Times New Roman",serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:"Times New Roman";mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:
none;mso-fareast-language:EN-IN;mso-bidi-language:HI">Young Talent Spotlight |
IBC Celebrity & Lifestyle</span></i><span style="font-size:12.0pt;
font-family:"Times New Roman",serif;mso-fareast-font-family:"Times New Roman";
mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:none;mso-fareast-language:EN-IN;mso-bidi-language:
HI"></span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:auto;mso-margin-bottom-alt:auto;
line-height:normal"><b><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:"Times New Roman",serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:"Times New Roman";mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:
none;mso-fareast-language:EN-IN;mso-bidi-language:HI">Standfirst:</span></b><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:"Times New Roman",serif;mso-fareast-font-family:
"Times New Roman";mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:none;mso-fareast-language:
EN-IN;mso-bidi-language:HI"> Nine years old and in Grade 3, Omansh Gupta is
just starting to discover what it feels like to own a room. His first steps on
a ramp came in a school classroom turned catwalk. Now he has a talent hunt
behind him, and plenty of curiosity left.</span></p>

<div class="MsoNormal" align="center" style="margin-bottom:0cm;text-align:center;
line-height:normal"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:"Times New Roman",serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:"Times New Roman";mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:
none;mso-fareast-language:EN-IN;mso-bidi-language:HI">

<hr size="1" width="100%" align="center">

</span></div>

<p class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:auto;mso-margin-bottom-alt:auto;
line-height:normal"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:"Times New Roman",serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:"Times New Roman";mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:
none;mso-fareast-language:EN-IN;mso-bidi-language:HI">Every fashion story has a
first moment, a single walk that changes how a person sees themselves. For
Omansh Gupta, it came at school.</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:auto;mso-margin-bottom-alt:auto;
line-height:normal"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:"Times New Roman",serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:"Times New Roman";mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:
none;mso-fareast-language:EN-IN;mso-bidi-language:HI">The occasion was a
Trash-to-Fashion competition, where everyday discards were reimagined as
wearable ideas. Omansh stepped onto the ramp for the very first time. The
lights, the audience and the quiet before the first step all arrived at once,
and he walked anyway. What began as a school activity became his first real
taste of style, self-expression and the thrill of the stage.</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:auto;mso-margin-bottom-alt:auto;
line-height:normal"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:"Times New Roman",serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:"Times New Roman";mso-font-kerning:0pt;mso-ligatures:
none;mso-fareast-language:EN-IN;mso-bidi-language:HI">That spark led him to <b>IBC
Super Kids</b>, a modelling talent hunt for children aged 3 to 12. There,
Omansh stood among young hopefuls from different backgrounds and got his first
experience of a proper talent show: the preparation, the nerves and the
excitement of waiting in the wings. For a nine-year-old, it was a first look at
the wider world of fashion and entertainment.</span></p>

new to him. Omansh comes from an entrepreneurial family that runs its own event
business, so celebrations, stage setups and presentations have always been part
of his surroundings. Growing up near the craft of creating occasions may
explain how comfortable he looks when all eyes turn his way.</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:auto;mso-margin-bottom-alt:auto;

discovering who you are. Omansh is learning how to carry himself, how to hold

single show.</span></p>
